genre: Classic rock / pop party cover band
style_note: Paint The Square Pink (American Cancer Society / Making Strides), 11a–1p. A long-running Cincinnati party band playing classic rock and pop to a lunchtime charity crowd, in warm, drying air.
artist_profile: Snidely Whiplash is a Cincinnati cover band fronted by WCPO media personality Pete Scalia (vocals, keys) with his father Tony Scalia on guitar, 25-plus years on the circuit: the old Blue Note in Price Hill, Mt. Adams Pavilion, a residency at Jeff Ruby's, charity galas. Pete's roots are high-school KISS and Van Halen covers; the current set is rock, pop and crowd-favourite classics in top hats. Five players (two guitars, bass, keys, drums) and five vocal mics. For the mix that means a guitar-forward classic-rock band with a speaking-voice frontman: the lead vocal and the two guitars carry the show, the keys fill underneath, and nothing about this material wants a modern scooped kit or hyped top end.
room_context: FSQ at midday: open plaza, no room gain, KS21 arch carrying the bottom. Cuts at outdoor depth (−7/−8) on drums and cabs; keys hold −6 because a board's 250–300 is warmth, not mechanical mud. The air is DRY (43% falling to 27% RH over the set), the opposite of the humid August nights, so high end is lost over the throw: no hat/overhead fizz trims this time, baked presence peaks trimmed only −3, and the one HF boost on the show (hat +3 @ 8k) is legal because the SM81 is flat. All five vocals hold the FSQ template curve by Brian's call.

reverbs.settings: Decay 1.5s (factory) · PreDelay 24ms (factory) · VLF −19 (factory) · E/L Max Early · Late −6 dB (from Equal factory reference, raised for outdoors) · Late Rolloff 8000Hz (from 6400Hz factory)
reverbs.plugin_eq: LC 200Hz on the return; no HS. Ducker Reverb mode, Thr −22dB so Pete's between-song talking stays dry.
reverbs.why: The default for Pete's lead and the harmony stacks on the mid-tempo classic-rock material. A forward, dense plate reads as 'record' vocal on 70s/80s covers. Rolloff opened to 8k because the air is dry and eating top on its own.

reverbs.settings: Decay 1.1s (from 1.60s factory) · PreDelay 10ms (from 0 factory) · VLF −10 (factory) · E/L Max Early · Late −6 dB (from Equal factory reference) · Late Rolloff 8000Hz (factory)
reverbs.plugin_eq: LC 200Hz on the return; Ducker Reverb mode, Thr −20dB.
reverbs.why: The up-tempo option: the rockers and party singalongs where a plate tail smears the next downbeat. Pulled to 1.1s with 10ms pre-delay so consonants land dry.

reverbs.settings: Decay 1.4s (from 1.80s factory) · PreDelay 30ms (factory) · VLF −12 (from 0 factory) · E/L Max Early · Late −6 dB (from Equal factory reference) · Late Rolloff 7000Hz (from 6000Hz factory)
reverbs.plugin_eq: LC 250Hz on the return to keep it off the chest; no ducker — it's for held notes.
reverbs.why: The ballad and power-ballad hall from the KB's rock table, for the slow numbers a covers set always carries. Decay cut well under factory because a noon plaza can't carry a long hall, and VLF pulled from 0 to −12 per the KB so the subs don't feed it.

reverbs.settings: Decay 1.0s (from 1.20s factory) · PreDelay 0 (factory) · VLF −9 (factory) · E/L Max Early · Late −6 dB (from Equal factory reference) · Late Rolloff 8000Hz (from 6800Hz factory)
reverbs.plugin_eq: LC 300Hz on the return so it never puts back the snare box ch 3 cuts at 450.
reverbs.why: Lives on the template's fader 10 SNARE PL8 return, so it costs nothing. Classic-rock backbeats earn a bright plate splash; 1.0s reads as crack, not room.

reverbs.settings: Decay 1.0s (from 1.20s factory) · PreDelay 0 (factory) · VLF −11 (factory) · E/L Max Early · Late −6 dB (from Equal factory reference) · Late Rolloff 5200Hz (factory)
reverbs.plugin_eq: LC 250Hz; leave the baked 300ms slap in — it's the point.
reverbs.why: For guitar solos on the KISS/Van Halen-lineage material: the KB's British guitar room with its built-in slap gives a lead line size without a hall. Send from whichever guitar is soloing.

reverb_pairing: Vocal Plate is the default and stays up; Vocal Chamber replaces it on the fast party numbers and Gold Hall on ballads. Pick one per song and keep it the same across all five vocals, so the picture doesn't move when a harmony comes in. Snare Plate A sits low under everything; its 300 LC and the vocal returns' 200–250 LC keep them apart. Guitar Room comes up only for solos. Studio A is the lowest send in the set. At noon on a dry plaza, start with Vocal Plate up modestly, Snare Plate barely up and the rest off until the set asks for them.

channels.name: Kick
channels.notes: Only kick mic (sheet's Kick In on ch 1 is blank). Inside, off-centre toward the beater.
channels.mic_notes: Tape Op: peaks at 60 Hz, 4 kHz and 10 kHz, with 750 Hz about 15 dB down. The thump and the beater are already built in, so there's no boost anywhere. The box cut sits at 300, where PSW engineers cut a D6, well below the baked 750 scoop so it doesn't dig deeper into a hole the capsule already has. Dynamics: no gate (a single kick mic in a covers set; the D6 rejects well). COMP: Red, 4:1, fast, 2–3 dB GR target to steady the four-on-the-floor numbers.
channels.eq_summary: One mic has to do inside and outside here, so the D6 keeps both of its humps: 60 Hz for the arch and 4k for the beater. The only move is −7 @ 300 to take out the box a plaza PA exaggerates. LPF 10k only shades the 10k fizz edge. In dry air the top doesn't need more help than that.

channels.name: Snare
channels.notes: Top only — no bottom mic (ch 4 blank), so wires come from this mic.
channels.mic_notes: SOS: +9 dB @ 5.5 kHz and +5 dB @ 150 Hz, which is the body the KB says beats the e604 outdoors. The crack is baked in, so it's trimmed −3 and never boosted. Only −3 because dry air takes top off over the throw anyway. Body at 150 left alone. GATE: none (it would chop ghost notes on shuffles). COMP: Green 4:1 fast attack-release, 3 dB GR.
channels.eq_summary: A fat classic-rock backbeat: keep the i5's 150 body, cut the 450 box at outdoor depth, and shave the baked 5.5k peak by only 3 dB since the plaza air is doing the rest. HPF 90 sheds the kick bleed. The snare plate on fader 10 adds the splash.

channels.name: Hat
channels.notes: SM81 LF switch ASSUMED FLAT, pad OUT. If found on the 18 dB/oct step, drop the desk HPF to 200.
channels.mic_notes: Shure user guide: flat 20 Hz–20 kHz with no presence peak, so the +3 @ 8k boosts cymbal, not a capsule bump. That's the one HF boost on the show, and it's there because dry air drops sizzle over the throw. −6 @ 400 is snare bleed; −7 @ 900 is stick clank.
channels.eq_summary: The hat owns the 8k sizzle for this kit (the overheads are left flat above 3k and sit at HPF 300). HPF 250 plus the 400 cut keep the snare from arriving twice, and −7 @ 900 takes the clank so it reads as a hat, not a stick.

channels.name: Rack 1
channels.notes: Template gate ON (native, not patched by us). Sizes not notated; if the sheet's racks/floor don't match the kit, move the gate sidechain at the desk.
channels.mic_notes: Audix chart: ~+5 dB at 150–200, a sag to ~+2 through 500 Hz–1 kHz, and ~+5/+6 presence at 4–7k. PSW calls it edgy. The box cut is at 400, below the baked sag, and the stick trim is at 6000 in the top of the presence bump. GATE: template native gate on 6/7/8 (thr −36, rel 227 ms). Leave it, and open the release if long fills get chopped.
channels.eq_summary: The small tom sits highest of the three: box lane 400 and stick lane 6000. The rack 2 and floor lanes step down from here, so three toms don't pile up in one octave on a fill.

channels.name: Rack 2
channels.notes: Template gate ON (native). Same mic as Rack 1, slotted lower.
channels.mic_notes: Same D2 figures as Rack 1. Slotting is by drum size: box at 350 and the presence trim at 4500 (the bottom of the D2's 4–7k bump). The two racks share nothing but depth.
channels.eq_summary: The middle tom: lanes at 350 and 4500, between Rack 1's 400 / 6000 and the floor's 300 / 5000. HPF 80 keeps a little more body than the small tom.

channels.name: Floor
channels.notes: Template gate ON (native, floor sidechain band).
channels.mic_notes: RecordingHacks (current Audix chart): +6 dB @ 5 kHz, a second peak above 10k, and rolloff below 70 Hz. That's why the 5k is trimmed and never boosted, and why the thud is left to the capsule instead of a low boost. PSW's 80 Hz 'woomp' notch isn't used: rock wants that thud.
channels.eq_summary: Deepest cut of the three toms (−8 @ 300) because the floor's muck is the one that fogs the bass. The 80–100 thud is untouched, and the baked 5k is trimmed −3.

channels.name: Overheads
channels.notes: STEREO on fader 9 — sheet listed OH R on 10, which is the SNARE PL8 return (protected). Pad ASSUMED OUT, LF switch flat.
channels.mic_notes: RecordingHacks: flat 60 Hz–3 kHz, with two peaks of +2 dB or less at 5.5k and 9k. The KB's 9k fizz trim came from a humid night. At 27–43% RH that trim would cut real cymbal air, so the top is left flat.
channels.eq_summary: Cymbals only: HPF 300 so the overheads don't duplicate the kick and toms, −7 @ 400 for bleed, and −5 @ 1200 for crash honk. Above 3k they're untouched. The hat channel owns the 8k sizzle.

channels.name: Bass DI
channels.notes: Only bass source (ch 12 cab mic blank). Plot shows the bass amp 'Direct'. The IMP sits between instrument and amp.
channels.mic_notes: Whirlwind: ±1 dB 20 Hz–20 kHz, nothing baked, so the +3 @ 800 is legal (a flat DI). No low boost: the kick's D6 owns 60 and the bass sits above it on the HPF 40. COMP: Purple (opto), 4:1, 3–4 dB GR for note-to-note evenness.
channels.eq_summary: The DI carries the whole low end, so it stays round. −7 @ 250 clears the mud the two guitars and keys also live in, and +3 @ 800 lets the line read on the tops for people far from the subs. LPF 5k drops the string clack a DI exaggerates.

channels.name: Guitar 1
channels.notes: Hang over the grille, off-centre. Locker fork: SM57 offered on Guitar 2, Brian kept both e609s.
channels.mic_notes: Sennheiser: ~+3 dB lift 2.5–6k centred near 4k. GUITAR 1 OWNS THE TOP LANE: the 4k lift is kept, and only the 6k fizz above it is trimmed. −3 @ 1800 leaves the upper mids to Guitar 2.
channels.eq_summary: Two e609s means the capsules can't separate the guitars, so the EQ does. Guitar 1 keeps its 4k presence and gives up a little at 1800. Guitar 2 does the opposite. Box −8 @ 400 is outdoor depth. If Tony's lead is on 14, swap the two curves at soundcheck.

channels.name: Guitar 2
channels.notes: Hang over the grille, off-centre. Kept on e609 (locker fork declined).
channels.mic_notes: Same e609 lift as Guitar 1. GUITAR 2 OWNS THE MID LANE: the lift is cut at 3500, inside the capsule's own bump, so Guitar 1's presence stands in front. The 1–2k honk is left alone for this guitar to live in. Box at 300 vs Guitar 1's 400.
channels.eq_summary: The mid-lane guitar: −5 @ 3500 hands the presence to Guitar 1, its 1–2k is left alone, and the box cut sits a third lower than Guitar 1's. LPF 8k keeps it behind. Nothing on these two curves matches.

channels.name: Keys L
channels.notes: Stereo per Brian (plot said '1 KEYS'). If only one line arrives, use 17 and leave 18.
channels.mic_notes: IMP ±1 dB, so there's no transducer to correct. The board is finished audio. One trim where it overlaps the guitars and bass. Identical to Keys R by design.
channels.eq_summary: Pete's keys fill under two guitars. −6 @ 300 makes room without thinning a piano or organ patch. The venue rule would say −8, but a board's 300 is warmth, not mud. HPF 50 keeps the left hand.

channels.name: Keys R
channels.mic_notes: Right half of the same board: identical curve to 17 so the stereo image doesn't tilt.
channels.eq_summary: Same as Keys L. Two halves of one instrument.
